recA5BnM5umys9yRk.Body: Kyle and Serena Denton are community herbalists creating wild-crafted and organic plant medicines out of Milwaukee since 2015. These products work—not in the allopathic "pharma-medicine" way, but in a terrain-support, consciousness bolstering plant-teacher sort of way.

Its extended handle lets you glide it smoothly across the face, neck, and body, and practitioners and users regularly report support for relaxation, circulation, and nervous system regulation. It's the same fork Chance uses in his own sessions, and a great entry point if you want to bring this work into your own daily routine.

I use LotusWei Elixirs to give me an edge with psychic & energetic sensitivity, discernment, and life force coherence. recMVdJjP2VZJyI2m.Body: Clive de Carle has spent decades researching high-quality natural health essentials, from magnesium and fulvic minerals to iodine, selenium, and vegan-sourced vitamin D. His supplements are formulated with a focus on bioavailability, so the body can actually absorb and use what you're taking rather than letting it pass through unused. It's a simple, no-nonsense approach to filling the nutritional gaps most modern diets leave behind.

rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Bio: Chance Garton is the host and producer of the Innerverse Podcast, where for over a decade he has investigated consciousness, mythology, symbolism, terrain health, and the psychosomatic language of the human body and mind. A biofield tuning practitioner, he uses tuning forks to help clients resolve physical symptoms, break negative patterns, and return to energetic coherence.
rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Name: Chance Garton
rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Role: Host of the Innerverse Podcast, biofield tuning practitioner & researcher

recQOLj1bGHrs7YCW.Bio: Michelle Lundquist describes herself as a folk herbalist, gardener and homemaker with a passion for plants and their ability to heal. She has studied and actively worked with herbs since 2013, drawing most of her knowledge from hands on experience and mentors of the wise woman tradition, and a do it yourself spirit runs through her work as she encourages people to take their wellbeing into their own hands. She hosted more than eighty episodes of The Healing Home podcast as a kitchen witch, homemaker and folk herbalist, and now co-hosts Symbolic Studies with her husband Mario Garza.
recQOLj1bGHrs7YCW.Name: Michelle Lundquist

recbqsYSV8FGvCA28.Bio: Kyle Denton is a community herbalist and medicine maker from Wisconsin who founded Tippecanoe Herbs with his wife Serena Marinelli in 2015. From their Milwaukee apothecary they craft small batch remedies from locally harvested and organic herbs, working from a bio terrain philosophy that blends Ayurveda with Western herbalism. He also runs Root Radical Herbal Academy, has taught for over a decade through his annual three season class and his Milwaukee herb walks, and sees clients as the Tuning Herbalist, using tuning forks to read the biofield. His Substack and podcast, Resonature, explore the interval between vital herbalism, biofield tuning and cosmology.
recbqsYSV8FGvCA28.Name: Kyle Denton
recbqsYSV8FGvCA28.Role: Community herbalist, founder of Tippecanoe Herbs

reckIvJxU4wRhybxA.Bio: Mario Garza is the artist and researcher behind Symbolic Studies, a project sharing symbolic insights on the zodiac, mythology, folklore and world religions, with astrology as its foundation. A lifelong artist who has worked as an art director and graphic designer for nearly 25 years, he runs Symbolic Studies from the Pacific Northwest alongside his wife Michelle, who co-hosts the podcast with him. His work traces syncretic threads across tarot, occultism and comparative religion, including the argument that the major deities of antiquity were originally polar gods before a solar model was laid over them. He also offers symbolic birth chart and tarot readings, private lessons and freelance design.
reckIvJxU4wRhybxA.Name: Mario Garza

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Saturn Reconsidered: The Golden Age Ruler", "body": "Mario Garza argues that Saturn has been badly mishandled by the modern mind. Drawing on Rene Guenon, whose Fundamental Symbols and Lord of the World he credits repeatedly, Garza contends the last golden age was a hyperborean, northern, polar age with Saturn as its ruling planet, and that the solarization of everything flipped a benefic figure into a malefic one. He also raises the possibility of an earlier feminine Saturn, pointing to Kali and to Crone symbolism generally, and asks where the Crone's wisdom has gone. Chance Garton adds his own theory that Saturn and Jupiter were once a single polar luminary that later split."}, {"title": "Elder Folklore: Fire, Fairies and Forbidden Wood", "body": "Michelle Lundquist opens the elder lore with the taboo on burning elderwood, said to invite the devil into the home or leave you bewitched, and traces the old Anglo root of elder to Eller, meaning to kindle, noting the soft pith stems that were hollowed into bellows to stoke a fire. Kyle Denton adds the spirit of the tree, Hyldemoer or Mother Holda, whose berries are still called holda berries in Germany, plus the customs against elder near a window or in a child's cradle. Denton describes the Fay and Elementals as opposed to iron, and links it to the Italian saying tocca ferro, touch iron."}, {"title": "The Elder Wand, Voldemort and Encoded Astrology", "body": "Kyle Denton walks through the weave Chance Garton says first hooked him on Denton's Root Radical elder episode. Denton lays out Hyldemoer as hylde plus moer, mother elder, then drops the aspirate H and reads the u as a v to arrive at Voldemort, the villain who spends the Harry Potter books hunting the Elder Wand. Denton notes Dumbledore's first act with that wand was lighting a fire that would never go out, echoing the Persian fire towers Garton described earlier. Garton says he looked up the character birthdays and found the heroes skew Leo while the villains skew Capricorn."}, {"title": "The Elderberry Smear and the Anti Language", "body": "The panel returns to early 2020, when Lundquist says the message was don't take elderberry syrup, cytokine storm, and a whole campaign ran against it. Garton asks Denton why elder gets labeled antiviral by what he calls the green allopaths, and Denton unpacks how virology is taught: the ACE2 receptor model he once believed and explained himself, the culture recipe of green monkey kidney cells and fetal calf serum, and Tom Cowan asking whether anyone has actually seen those receptors. Denton argues the deeper problem is marketing, since it is easier to stamp anti on a bottle than to say what a plant is for."}, {"title": "Closing Weave: Boundaries, the Lost Center, Beauty in the Dark", "body": "In the final hour each guest lands the tree somewhere different. Denton frames elder as boundary medicine, a plant that thrives on hedgerows and fence rows and teaches discipline through the slow, patient work of taking berries off without crushing them until you return to that hollow center. Garza, citing Guenon again, says what the Dark Ages really concealed was the Supreme Center, the world axis, and that a returning golden age would be its return. Lundquist finds beauty in the darkness, calling a shot of black elderberry syrup a scrying mirror, and mentions dyeing fabric with the berries for ritual cloth."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Your favorite AstroHerbalism squad returns to the stage to deep dive into the granddaddy mother of all plant healers, the incredible Elder Tree. In this stream we will explore the medicinal qualities of elderberry and elderflower, the folk lore and culture inspired by this Saturnian superflora, and the Capricornian signatures it expresses. Kyle Denton of Tippecanoe Herbs, Michelle Lundquist of the Healing Home, Mario Garza of Symbolic Studies and Slick Dissident reprise their roles for another round of this groundbreaking Vibe Rant series!
